scoring_weights.note: Score = weighted peak contact force (w_head/w_pelvis/w_other) plus a tracking-error penalty, matching the reference doc's own optimizer (section 8.3: 'evaluate peak contact force ... lower is better') plus its section 8.2 minimum-jerk-trajectory safety requirement. There is deliberately NO separate reward for preventing the fall outright: every reference-doc principle (lower CoM, align impact zone, minimum-jerk transition) is about reducing injury from a fall that is already happening, not about avoiding the fall itself -- and a fully prevented fall already scores 0 on every force term (no contact occurs), which is already the best any peak-force sum can produce, so this objective already rewards prevention as strongly as physically possible without a separate term. tracking_error_penalty_per_rad IS a real, separate injury channel from ground impact (joint/actuator torque spikes from failing to follow the planned smooth path under load) -- applied to every triggered trial, recovered included, since that risk is independent of whether the fall itself is avoided. Each control point's recovery_rate (below) is reported for hardware go/no-go review -- the fraction of tested conditions where the pose prevented the fall entirely -- but is informational only and does not affect score.

velocity_estimate_source: base linear velocity magnitude (||qvel[0:3]||) measured at the instant the pose is triggered -- proxy for the Phase-2 TCN's Stage-3 velocity-regression output. Verify qvel[0:3] really is the free-joint base linear velocity against g1_pendulum.xml's actual joint ordering before trusting this in Phase 4/5.
actuator_scope: CMA-ES optimizes ONLY the 12 leg actuators (pose_ctrl's pendulum_roll/pendulum_pitch entries are pinned at their 'stand' keyframe value for every trial -- see actuator_group_ids). This rig's real-world target is a LOWER-LIMB-ONLY exoskeleton for paralyzed rehab patients: the hardware has no actuator on the wearer's own torso/head, so letting the optimizer command the pendulum (as every pose in pose_library_v5.json and earlier does) let it 'solve' head/pelvis impact by swinging that mass out of the way -- something no real wearer or exoskeleton can do. Confirmed visually in the MuJoCo viewer before this fix. Pinning removes the exploit but is NOT full passivity: the pendulum's high-kp position actuator still resists being pushed off 'stand' by the disturbance, acting like a stiff neck-brace rather than a truly floppy unsupported torso. A closer-to-real passive response would need an XML-level actuator-gain change -- flag with your mentor before making it, since it touches the shared model file every phase depends on. Every pose in this file was (re-)optimized under the leg-only scope; anything compared against pose_library_v5.json or earlier must be re-run, not diffed directly, since the search space itself changed.

impact_proxies.head: pendulum bob, contact enabled at runtime
impact_proxies.hands: NOT MODELED -- rig has no arms
impact_proxies.other: any other non-foot body (e.g. knee/hip) -- weighted lower than pelvis/head, but not free

open_questions_for_mentor: Spec says 6 actuated joints; this rig has model.nu actuators (14 on the real g1_pendulum.xml: 2 pendulum + 12 leg). This library outputs angles for every actuator on the loaded model -- confirm which joint set Stage 4 actually expects.
Lookup table is keyed on BOTH scenario_fn and category for 'cause' because it isn't yet confirmed which granularity the Phase 2 TCN's Cause-class output uses. Resolve before Phase 5.
